note: quince#111 face 1, and the state its deliberate-SIGKILL experiment produced and nothing could name. A watcher is RUNNING — it was a child of the session, a single-pid kill reparented it to init and it kept ticking — while the session that armed it is gone. For four minutes `status` reported `live` with the note 'nothing to do' about a watch that could wake nobody, and `owed` classifies from the same record, so a replacement session's Stop hook would have been satisfied by a watcher belonging to a dead session. That outcome was missed by two minutes of luck: the orphan exited at 13:30:07 and the replacement started at ~13:35. ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING here as it is for `starting`: `orphaned` must be evaluated before `starting`, because a session that dies seconds after arming leaves a watcher that is orphaned rather than starting — and `starting` is the one class that says 'do not arm a second one', which is exactly the wrong instruction when the first can wake nobody. Its mirrors: watch-orphan-unknown-owner-is-not-orphaned.json for the conservative direction, and watch-starting-is-neither-dead-nor-wedged.json for the neighbour it must not swallow.
expect: watch=orphaned state=STATE pid=4242 interval=60s last_watcher_tick=2026-07-27T13:26:00Z age=30s owner_pid=4200

note: this watcher is RUNNING and the session that armed it is GONE, so it can wake nobody. It is not live and it is not dead — `live` would tell you nothing is owed, `dead` would tell you to re-arm from a state a running process is still writing. Run `forge-watch stop` to end it, THEN re-arm from this state; do not reseed it.
